question: In an isosceles triangle ABC, AB = AC and AD is perpendicular to BC. If AD = 5 cm and the perimeter of ΔABC is 50 cm, then twice the length of BC (in cm) is:
solution:
**Given:**

ΔABC is an isosceles triangle

AB = AC

Perimeter = 50 cm

AD = 5 cm

**Formula used:**

Pythagoras Theorem:

Hypotenuse² = Perpendicular² + Base²

In an isosceles triangle if a perpendicular is drawn from a vertices to its opposite side then it will bisect the side into two equal parts 

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/aba95889639acdc723a272c6a67914791215207354a11363b883e0ac5e38209f.png] 

AD perpendicular to BC

So, ΔADB is right angle triangle

Let AB = AC be x and BD be y

BD = DC (AD will bisect BC)

Now,

x + x + y + y = 50

⇒ x + y = 25 

⇒ x = 25 - y

From ΔABD

x² = y² + 5²

⇒ (25 - y)² = y² + 5²

⇒ 625 - 50y + y² = y² + 25

⇒ 50y = 625 - 25

⇒ 50y = 600

⇒ y = 600/50 

⇒ y = 12

⇒ BD = 12

Now,

BC = 2 × BD [∵ In isosceles triangle, altitude and median are same]

BC = 2 × 12 = 24 cm

2BC = 24 × 2 = 48 cm

**∴ Twice the length of BC (in cm) is 48.**
